description: Stereo granular processor in four HP, chopping what comes in into short grains, with a chaotic signal generated inside it that can scatter where the grains are read from

params.text: Sets the length of each grain, 1ms at the bottom of its travel to 100ms at the top
Sets how often a new grain is started, one per second at the bottom of its travel to fifty-one per second at the top
Sets how far back in the recorded buffer the grains are read from
Crossfades between the signal coming in and the grains, 0% for the dry signal alone and 100% for the grains alone
Sets how deeply the chaotic signal scatters the grain positions and rate, 0% to 100%; above zero about a third of the grains also play backwards
Sets how fast the chaotic signal moves, a hundredth of its base speed to twice it

inputs.text: The left side of the signal to be granulated; with nothing patched to the right jack this one feeds both sides
The right side of the signal to be granulated
Added to the SIZE knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the BREAK knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the SHIFT knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the MIX knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the CHAOS knob, ten points per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to the RATE knob, a fifth of the base speed per volt; the total is held between a hundredth of it and twice it

outputs.text: The left side of the grains, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The right side of the grains, crossfaded with the dry signal by MIX
The chaotic signal itself, ±5V, at the speed set by RATE; the CHAOS knob does not dim it
The chaotic signal sampled and held ten times per unit of the RATE setting, ±5V; the CHAOS knob does not dim it

notes: with CHAOS above zero and BREAK past seven tenths of its travel, a fifth of the grains are also dropped or raised by an octave at random.
place this immediately to the right of a YAMANOTE and cables appear on their own: YAMANOTE's send A into the two input jacks, and the two output jacks into its return A.
placing it to the right of another Runner, Facehugger or Ovomorph that is itself beside a YAMANOTE cables it to that YAMANOTE's send and return B instead.
sixteen grains can sound at once; new grains are dropped while all sixteen are busy, so a long SIZE with a high BREAK thins out rather than piling up.
